It is accusative, an exception not from the first [category] (a disjoined exception), as He said: ﴿فَإنَّهم عَدُوٌّ لِي إلا رَبَّ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 77]. The meaning is: but Iblīs refused to be [among them].

zajjaj:32-32.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قالَ يا إبْلِيسُ ما لَكَ ألا تَكُونَ مَعَ السّاجِدِينَ﴾: the position of ”أنْ“ is accusative, by dropping ”فِي“ and the governing word reaching through to ”أنْ“ (accusative by removal of the preposition). The meaning is: "what is the matter with you in not being with those who prostrate?"

zajjaj:34-34.t: And His saying: ﴿فَإنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ﴾ means: "stoned, accursed".

zajjaj:44-44.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَها سَبْعَةُ أبْوابٍ لِكُلِّ بابٍ مِنهم جُزْءٌ مَقْسُومٌ﴾: Hell has seven levels; for each level is a class of those who are punished, according to their rank in sin.

zajjaj:47-47.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَـزَعْنا ما في صُدُورِهِمْ مِن غِلٍّ﴾: ”اَلْغِلُّ“ is rancour. It is related that the believers will be delivered from the Fire and held on a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, and retribution will be exacted for some of them from others; then they will be ordered to Paradise, having been cleansed and refined, so that their intentions are purified of rancour. ﴿إخْوانًا﴾ is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿عَلى سُرُرٍ مُتَقابِلِينَ﴾: in the exegesis: none of them looks at the back of another's head.

zajjaj:48-48.t: ﴿لا يَمَسُّهم فِيها نَصَبٌ﴾, i.e. no fatigue will touch them.

zajjaj:49-49.t: ﴿أنِّي أنا الغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ ﴿وَأنَّ عَذابِي هو العَذابُ الألِيمُ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 50]: it is related in the exegesis that if the servant knew the extent of Allah's pardon, he would not refrain from any sin; and if he knew the measure of His punishment, he would wear himself out in worship and would not venture upon any sin.

zajjaj:52-52.t:
﴿فَقالُوا سَلامًا﴾, he said: "Peace" [Translator's note: the source quotes قالَ: سَلامٌ, which belongs to the parallel verse, not to this one]. ”سَلامًا“ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), as though they said: "we greet [you] with a greeting of peace".
And His saying: ﴿قالَ إنّا مِنكم وجِلُونَ﴾, i.e. afraid. He only became afraid when he set the calf before them and saw them not eating of it; [then] he became afraid.

zajjaj:53-53.t: ﴿قالُوا لا تَوْجَلْ﴾: one says ”وَجِلَ، يَوْجَلُ، وياجَلُ، يَيْجَلُ، ويِيْجَلُ“ when one fears.

zajjaj:54-54.t:
﴿فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ﴾, with fatḥa on the nūn, which is better in reading. And it was read: ”فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونِ“ with kasra on the nūn — Nāfiʿ read it so. The original is ”فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَنِ“; the two nūns were felt to be heavy, so one of them was dropped. It has also been said that the dropping is from assimilation, as though it were ”فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُنَّ“ [Translator's note: so in the source, presumably تُبَشِّرُونِّ] with a doubled nūn, and then one of the two nūns was dropped because of the heaviness of the doubling, as they said ”رُبَّما“ and ”رُبَما“. The poet said, on dropping the nūn:
؎رَأتْهُ كالنَّعامِ يُعَلُّ مِسْكًا يَسُوءُ الغالِياتِ إذا فَلَيْنِي
(She saw it [white] like ostriches, being drenched again and again with musk — it vexes the women who perfume when they search my hair.)
He means ”فَلَيْنَنِي“.

zajjaj:56-56.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يَقْنَطُ مِن رَحْمَةِ رَبِّهِ﴾: one says ”قَنَطَ، يَقْنِطُ“ and ”قَنِطَ، يَقْنَطُ“; both are permissible. ”اَلْقُنُوطُ“ means ”اَلْيَأْسُ“ (despair).

zajjaj:57-57.t: ﴿قالَ فَما خَطْبُكُمْ﴾, i.e. so what is your business?

zajjaj:59-59.t: And His saying: ﴿إلا آلَ لُوطٍ﴾ is an exception not from the first [category] (a disjoined exception). The meaning is: ﴿قالُوا إنّا أُرْسِلْنا إلى قَوْمٍ مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 58] ﴿إلا آلَ لُوطٍ إنّا لَمُنَجُّوهم أجْمَعِينَ﴾; the meaning is: we have been sent with the punishment to the people of Lūṭ.

zajjaj:60-60.t:
And His saying: ﴿إلا امْرَأتَهُ قَدَّرْنا إنَّها لَمِنَ الغابِرِينَ﴾: the meaning is: "We knew that she is among those who remain behind". It has been said: "We arranged that she is among those who remain behind". But ”قَدَّرْنا“ here needs no explanation; the meaning is: "except his wife — We decreed that she is among those remaining in the punishment". ”اَلْغابِرُ“ is the one who remains. The poet said:
؎فَما ونى مُحَمَّدٌ مُذْ أنْ غَفَرْ لَهُ الإلَهُ ما مَضى وما غَبَرْ
(Muḥammad has not slackened since God forgave him what has passed and what remains.)
The meaning is: and what remains.

zajjaj:63-63.t: And His saying: ﴿بِما كانُوا فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ﴾, i.e. we have come to you with the punishment about whose descent they used to doubt.

zajjaj:65-65.t: And His saying: ﴿فَأسْرِ بِأهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾: you say ”فَأسْرِ بِأهْلِكَ“ with the disjunctive alif (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) and with the conjunctive alif (hamzat al-waṣl); of travelling by night one says both ”أسْرى“ and ”سَرى“. The meaning of ”بِقِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ“ is: after a good part of the night has passed. ﴿وَلا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكم أحَدٌ﴾: he ﷺ was commanded not to turn round, so that he would not see the enormity of the punishment descending on them — and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:66-66.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أنَّ دابِرَ هَؤُلاءِ مَقْطُوعٌ مُصْبِحِينَ﴾: the position of ”أنَّ“ is accusative, and it is a badal (substitute) for His saying: ﴿وَقَضَيْنا إلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ الأمْرَ﴾; then He explained what the matter is. So the meaning is "and We conveyed to him the decree that the last remnant of these would be cut off in the morning". ”مُصْبِحِينَ“ is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).

zajjaj:68-68.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ هَؤُلاءِ ضَيْفِي﴾: ”اَلضَّيْفُ“ is kept singular even when a group is described by it. You say ”هَذا ضَيْفٌ“, ”هَذانِ ضَيْفٌ“ and ”هَؤُلاءِ ضَيْفٌ“, just as you say ”هَؤُلاءِ عَدْلٌ“; and if you wish you say ”أضْيافٌ“ and ”ضِيفانٌ“. Whoever uses the singular does so because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with which the noun is described; that is why he uses the singular. The maṣdar is kept singular in your saying ”ضَرَبْتُ القَوْمَ ضَرْبًا“ ("I struck the people a striking") only because the striking is one kind; when it is of several kinds you put it in the dual or plural and say ”ضَرْبَتُهم ضَرْبَيْنِ“ [Translator's note: so printed; ضَرَبْتُهم is meant] and ”ضَرَبْتُهم ضُرُوبًا“, i.e. kinds of striking. ”اَلضَّيْفُ“ is the maṣdar of ”ضِفْتُ الرَّجُلَ، أضِيفُهُ، ضَيْفًا، فَأنا ضائِفٌ، والرَّجُلُ مَضِيفٌ“ ("I lodged as a guest with the man … so I am a guest (ḍāʾif) and the man is the one guested upon") when he is the object; and ”أضَفْتُهُ“ when I gave him lodging.
